decisions.SUFFICIENT: Every parsed core point is SUPPORTED; explicitly requested attributes are present.
decisions.PARTIAL: At least one point is SUPPORTED or PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED; documentation permits incomplete core points or requested attributes. Runtime marks a point PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED at lexical score >= 0.18 with no missing extracted entity, even when requested attributes are missing.
decisions.NOT_SUPPORTED: Point-level status used when score < partial threshold or an extracted entity is missing.
decisions.INSUFFICIENT: No point supported, retrieval/input failure, or detected evidence conflict; sends REQUIRE_REFUSAL.
decisions.REFUSAL: Not an Evidence decision enum; downstream behavior for INSUFFICIENT/BLOCKED.

answers_to_questions.multiple_required_points: Yes. Any supported/partial point yields PARTIAL when not all are fully supported.
answers_to_questions.single_point_incomplete: Yes in implementation: a single point can be PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED from lexical score >= 0.18.
answers_to_questions.missing_entity: No for extracted entities, but the extractor only recognizes organization-like patterns and does not model degree/scope/value constraints.
answers_to_questions.missing_attribute: Yes: implementation allows PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED despite missing requested attributes; README describes this as an incomplete PARTIAL.
answers_to_questions.evidence_supports_only_part: Yes, if the runtime calls that point usable support.
answers_to_questions.unresolved_qualifier: Underspecified; only configured attribute conflicts and current-status checks are explicit.
answers_to_questions.partial_enters_answer_generation: Yes. PARTIAL maps to ALLOW_PARTIAL_ANSWER and Answer permits only supported/PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED mapped units.
answers_to_questions.partial_answer_scope: Citation/Answer contracts prohibit exposing unsupported point units, but they do not redefine the Evidence point threshold.
answers_to_questions.boundary: INSUFFICIENT requires no support, conflict, or validation failure; PARTIAL is a lexical proxy boundary, not semantic entailment.
